title: "tsrs shadow type-check"
description: "Evaluation, shadow CI job and promotion criteria for tsrs, the Rust port of the TypeScript 7 compiler."
updatedAt: "2026-10-23"
---

## Decision

[tsrs](https://github.com/oxc-project/tsrs) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7
compiler built with the TypeScript team and planned to become part of Oxc. It is
**experimental**. `tsc` (TypeScript 7.0.2) stays the required type-check gate.
tsrs runs in two advisory places only:

1. The [pre-push gate](/build/development-tools/pre-push-checks) defaults to tsc.
   Explicit `--checker tsrs` comparisons are advisory and always confirmed by
   tsc, including a tsrs pass. Resolution requires a planned qualified project;
   hook mode accepts only an existing `TSRS_BIN` and never fetches packages.
   Clean-source parity alone does not qualify detection of seeded errors.
2. `.github/workflows/tsrs-shadow.yaml` compares tsrs with `tsc` on main pushes
   that touch qualified projects and reports differences as warnings. The job is
   `continue-on-error` and is not a required check.

The pin is `tsrs@0.18.0-ts7.1.0-dev.20260929` (version string
`7.1.0-dev.20260930.4`). It is installed outside the workspace (`npm install
--prefix` in CI, the `npm exec` cache locally) so the shadow never changes
`bun.lock`. Set `TSRS_BIN` to use a different binary locally.

## Evaluation (2026-10-23)

Median of three cold runs per checker on a 10-core, 24 GB Apple Silicon machine,
`-p <project> --noEmit --incremental false --composite false`, queued through
`ttr resources run`. Workspace `dist` declarations were not built (builds are
CI-only), so absolute diagnostic counts include missing-module noise; parity is
still meaningful because every checker saw the same files. Timings were taken
while other sessions shared the machine, so treat them as relative.

| Project | tsc 7.0.2 | tsc 7.1.0-beta | tsrs | Speedup vs 7.0 | Diagnostics 7.0 / tsrs | Exact parity vs 7.0 | Location parity vs 7.0 | Location parity vs 7.1-beta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/types` (build config) | 0.49 s / 349 MB | 0.36 s / 232 MB | 0.22 s / 111 MB | 2.2x | 0 / 0 | yes | yes | yes |
| `packages/utils` | 0.64 s / 1411 MB | 0.56 s / 1107 MB | 0.24 s / 429 MB | 2.7x | 155 / 155 | yes | yes | yes |
| `packages/ui` | 1.79 s / 1954 MB | 1.51 s / 1249 MB | 0.57 s / 665 MB | 3.1x | 1018 / 1038 | no | no | yes |
| `packages/supabase` | 0.29 s / 268 MB | 0.27 s / 211 MB | 0.19 s / 115 MB | 1.5x | 8 / 8 | yes | yes | yes |
| `packages/internal-api` | 0.26 s / 174 MB | 0.24 s / 136 MB | 0.20 s / 77 MB | 1.3x | 84 / 84 | yes | yes | yes |
| `apps/tasks` | 2.70 s / 2595 MB | 2.10 s / 2158 MB | 0.64 s / 860 MB | 4.2x | 2013 / 2013 | no | yes | yes |
| `apps/calendar` | 2.42 s / 3321 MB | 3.77 s / 2341 MB | 0.78 s / 1000 MB | 3.1x | 1622 / 1622 | no | yes | yes |
| `apps/web` | 21.4 s / 3803 MB | 23.6 s / 3968 MB | 3.4 s / 1866 MB | 6.3x | 2296 / 2314 | no | no | yes |
| **Total** | 30.0 s | 32.4 s | 6.2 s | 4.8x | | | | |

"Exact" compares the full diagnostic multiset including message text,
independent of order. "Location" compares file, line, column and code.

Findings:

- **tsrs matches TypeScript 7.1, not 7.0.** Every difference from 7.0.2 also
  appears with `tsc` 7.1.0-beta. `packages/ui` and `apps/web` gain implicit-`any`
  diagnostics under 7.1 semantics; `apps/tasks` and `apps/calendar` differ only in
  how long types are printed. Against 7.1-beta, tsrs has location parity on all
  eight projects and exact parity on seven; `apps/web` differs in two messages
  where tsrs prints a truncated property type instead of `...`.
- **Speed and memory.** tsrs is 1.3-6.3x faster (larger projects gain more) with
  roughly 50-70% less peak memory.
- **TypeScript 7.1 beta** is 1.1-1.3x faster than 7.0.2 on packages and
  `apps/tasks`, but slower on `apps/calendar` and `apps/web` in this run, with
  lower memory. It is a beta and changes diagnostics, so it is not adopted.
- **Configuration support.** All tsconfig features we use type-check the same:
  package-name `extends` chains, `paths`, `NodeNext`/`Bundler` resolution, `jsx`
  `preserve`/`react-jsx`, `types`, `lib` including `webworker`, JSON modules and
  `include` globs. `--build --dry` resolves the same project-reference graph for
  `apps/meet` and `apps/web`. `--showConfig` is **not supported**. Emit
  (declarations, `--build` writes) was not evaluated because it is a build.
- **Exit status** is 2 for diagnostics where `tsc` 7.0.2 returns 1; compare
  success versus failure, not exact codes.

## Shadow job

`node scripts/ci/tsrs-shadow.js` runs both checkers per project, records wall
time and peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time`), compares diagnostic multisets and writes a
step summary, `::warning` annotations (up to 20 per side) and a JSON report kept
for 30 days. The default project list is the parity-qualified set: `packages/types`,
`packages/utils`, `packages/supabase`, `packages/internal-api`, `apps/tasks` and
`apps/calendar`. CI builds the workspace declarations first, exactly like the
required type-check, so CI parity is the authoritative evidence. Pull requests run
the job only when the shadow tooling changes; `workflow_dispatch` runs it on demand.

```bash
node scripts/ci/tsrs-shadow.js --tsrs <path-to-tsrs> --project apps/web/tsconfig.json
```

The local flag runs tsrs only for projects in `TSRS_PROJECTS`, even when one
workspace has both qualified and unqualified configs. Tsc still checks every
project. Exact diagnostic-key multiset differences are printed as advisory
`tsrs-only` / `tsc-only` output, including when tsc passes; a shadow mismatch
never changes the authoritative tsc result.

## Promotion criteria

Do not replace `tsc` as the required gate until **all** of these hold:

1. **Version alignment.** The pinned tsrs release tracks the same TypeScript
   minor as the repository gate (or the repository adopts the matching stable
   TypeScript minor), and is a non-`dev` release pinned exactly through the
   owning workspace's package manager with a reviewed lockfile change.
2. **Parity over time.** At least 30 consecutive shadow runs on main per
   promoted project show location parity, matching success/failure status and no
   tsrs crash, with warm declarations. Message-text differences are reviewed and
   recorded. Each promoted project must also have a seeded-error corpus that
   both checkers reject, covering real type errors, path/ambient declarations
   and reference boundaries. Until then, keep tsc confirmation on passes too.
3. **Feature coverage.** Every project the required job checks is covered,
   including project references (`apps/meet`), worker/boundary configs and
   declaration-emitting builds, or an explicit `tsc` fallback is kept for each
   unsupported feature.
4. **Operational evidence.** Linux CI wall time and memory are recorded for the
   promoted set, and rollback is a single-commit switch back to `tsc`.

Keep tsrs advisory, with tsc confirming every outcome, until all criteria hold.
Then switch only the qualified scopes, preserving explicit tsc fallbacks and
emit tasks. Update this page, the project list in `scripts/ci/tsrs-shadow.js`
and the [pre-push gate](/build/development-tools/pre-push-checks) together.
